outcome.technical: (a) tests/test_run_agent_session.py: STREAM_TABLE has five literal streams (two paired stretches; one init with two results; paired stretches with the last result repeated under one uuid; a single stretch; no result). Each row holds the runner's recorded figures, the names it records as absent, and tools/stream-cost.py's (duration_ms, num_turns, paired), all as values. _table_cases runs each row through the real runner (new stub switch STUB_STREAM writes a stream file verbatim) and through the tool, and asserts both (ras79). The repeated-uuid row showed the runner counting one event twice, so the runner now follows the tool there: read_stream skips an event whose string uuid it has already read. The comment in run-agent-session.py that claimed one shared pairing rule differing in one case is replaced: it states only the runner's rule (dedupe by uuid, a stretch told by its init, per-stretch sums only when inits and results pair) and why that is the stricter reading, and it names STREAM_TABLE / ras79 for how the tool reads the same streams. (b) A new _parse_line catches any exception json.loads raises. Both stream readers in the runner use it (read_stream counts the line as unparsed; invoked_skills skips it), since a RecursionError escaping either ended the runner after the session ran. The could-not-run tail now says 'could not be parsed as JSON', not 'were not JSON', because a too-deep line is JSON. The fixture _too_deep() steps the depth up until this interpreter really raises RecursionError: Python 3.14 parses a line 100000 deep, measured here, and fails at 1000000 with 'Stack overflow'. The line reaches the stub as a file because megabytes overflow an environment variable (E2BIG on the first try).
